# lucidity Provider

Interact with the Lucidity cloud storage optimization platform.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    lucidity = {
      source = "registry.terraform.io/luciditycloud/lucidity"
    }
  }
}

# Authenticate as a user, with a refresh token generated in the dashboard.
provider "lucidity" {
  lucidity_dashboard_url          = "https://www.web.lucidity.dev/dashboard"
  lucidity_dashboard_account_name = "Acme Corp"

  # The refresh token itself is best supplied via refresh_token_file,
  # refresh_token_command, or the LUCIDITY_REFRESH_TOKEN environment
  # variable rather than hardcoded here — see the provider index docs.
}

# Or authenticate as a service account (recommended for automation). The
# client secret is shown only once, when the credential is created.
provider "lucidity" {
  alias                           = "service_account"
  lucidity_dashboard_url          = "https://www.web.lucidity.dev/dashboard"
  lucidity_dashboard_account_name = "Acme Corp"

  client_id             = "svc-abc123"
  client_secret_command = "aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id lucidity/client-secret --query SecretString --output text"
  # or LUCIDITY_CLIENT_ID + LUCIDITY_CLIENT_SECRET in the environment
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `lucidity_dashboard_account_name` (String) The Lucidity dashboard account the credentials (refresh token or service account) are expected to belong to. Intended to catch a wrong-account refresh token before any tenant operation runs; the provider cannot yet cross-validate this against the token itself (no Lucidity endpoint currently exposes which account a token belongs to), so today this is recorded but not enforced.
- `lucidity_dashboard_url` (String) The URL you use to log in to the Lucidity dashboard. Determines the API base URL the provider talks to — there is no separate base-URL setting. Must be exactly one of: https://www.web.lucidity.dev/dashboard, https://web-azurepls.lucidity.cloud/dashboard, https://app.lucidity.cloud, https://in.app.lucidity.cloud, https://eu.app.lucidity.cloud.

### Optional

- `client_id` (String) Client ID of a Lucidity service account credential, for authenticating as a service account instead of a user. Can also be set with the LUCIDITY_CLIENT_ID environment variable. Requires a client secret (client_secret, client_secret_file, client_secret_command, or LUCIDITY_CLIENT_SECRET). Can't be combined with a refresh token.
- `client_secret` (String, Sensitive) Client secret of a Lucidity service account credential, supplied directly. Discouraged for the same reason as refresh_token; prefer client_secret_file, client_secret_command, or the LUCIDITY_CLIENT_SECRET environment variable. At most one of client_secret, client_secret_file, or client_secret_command may be set.
- `client_secret_command` (String) Shell command whose trimmed stdout is used as the service account client secret, e.g. `aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id lucidity/client-secret --query SecretString --output text`. Runs via the platform shell with a 30s timeout; stdout is never logged. At most one of client_secret, client_secret_file, or client_secret_command may be set.
- `client_secret_file` (String) Path to a local file containing only the service account client secret; its contents are trimmed of surrounding whitespace. At most one of client_secret, client_secret_file, or client_secret_command may be set.
- `max_parallel_requests` (Number) Maximum number of concurrent Lucidity API requests. Defaults to 10.
- `proactive_refresh_buffer_minutes` (Number) How many minutes before the 15-minute access-token expiry to proactively renew it. Defaults to 3. Must be between 1 and 14.
- `refresh_token` (String, Sensitive) Long-lived Lucidity refresh token for a user, supplied directly (format <accessKey>.<secretKey>, generated in the dashboard). Discouraged: the value ends up in your .tf config or, if fed from a data source, in Terraform state. Prefer refresh_token_file, refresh_token_command, or the LUCIDITY_REFRESH_TOKEN environment variable. At most one of refresh_token, refresh_token_file, or refresh_token_command may be set, and not together with service account credentials (client_id / client_secret*).
- `refresh_token_command` (String) Shell command whose trimmed stdout is used as the Lucidity refresh token, e.g. `vault kv get -field=token secret/lucidity`. Runs via the platform shell with a 30s timeout; stdout is never logged, including at TF_LOG=DEBUG. At most one of refresh_token, refresh_token_file, or refresh_token_command may be set.
- `refresh_token_file` (String) Path to a local file containing only the Lucidity refresh token; its contents are trimmed of surrounding whitespace. Never sent anywhere but read into memory. At most one of refresh_token, refresh_token_file, or refresh_token_command may be set.
